newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian MPs pass controversial new election law.
newsitem.headline: Albanian MPs pass controversial new election law.

text.p: Albania's parliament passed a controversial new election law on Tuesday, paving the way for elections to be held in June and prevent the country sliding once more into the chaos and rioting of February and March.

But the law was opposed by the second-largest party in parliament, the Socialist Party, which has threatened that it and other parties would walk out of the broad coalition government formed amid the March rioting if it was passed.

The law was expected to pave the way for new elections at the end of June and was part of a six-point political contract brokered by Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) envoy Franz Vrantizky last week.
The elections were seen as vital to stop Albania sliding back into the violence and rioting of February and March which came in the wake of the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.

The Socialists earlier accused the Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha, which has a majority in parliament, of trying to railroad a law through parliament which the other parties in government found unacceptable.

"We will also reconsider our participation in the government and also in the parliament (if this law passed). The passing of that draft will return the Albanian crisis back to that of before March 1997," Socialist Party Parliamentary Group chairman Namik Dokle told parliament.
